title: Incident 1520: Intermittent DNS Resolution Cascades & CoreDNS Throttling
problem_brief: During flash sales, downstream microservices report intermittent 'EAI_AGAIN (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND)' connection drops reaching 3.4% of API calls. Kubernetes worker node CPU is below 40%, but CoreDNS latency spiked to 2,400ms. Inspect the CoreDNS logs, conntrack table metrics, and pod /etc/resolv.conf search domains. Diagnose the root cause without guided hints, provide safe operational mitigation, and propose a resilient cluster DNS architecture.

entries.message: [OK] 2 api.stripe.com. A: NOERROR (5 queries fired for 1 external domain)
iptables conntrack: table full, dropping packet (ip_conntrack_max limit reached).

evidence_tabs.label: Pod /etc/resolv.conf & ndots Config
evidence_tabs.content:
```text
nameserver 10.96.0.10
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
options ndots:5
```
**Note:** Because `api.stripe.com` contains fewer than 5 dots (it has 2 dots), glibc appends each search domain sequentially before attempting the raw domain as an external FQDN, generating 4 unnecessary NXDOMAIN queries per external API call.

submission_fields.label: 1. Incident Timeline & Scope of Packet Loss
submission_fields.placeholder: Document timestamps, affected external API calls, and conntrack table saturation...
submission_fields.guidance: Focus on the relationship between traffic surges and DNS packet drops.

submission_fields.label: 2. Root Cause Hypothesis (ndots:5 vs conntrack table)
submission_fields.placeholder: Explain how default ndots:5 configuration generated an internal query explosion...
submission_fields.guidance: Distinguish verified CoreDNS NXDOMAIN logs from upstream ISP assumptions.

submission_fields.label: 3. Immediate Safe Mitigation Plan
submission_fields.placeholder: How will you alleviate DNS pressure and conntrack saturation right now?
submission_fields.guidance: Consider CoreDNS autoscale, sysctl conntrack limit, and trailing dot FQDNs.

submission_fields.label: 4. Verification & Health Confirmation
submission_fields.placeholder: What metrics confirm DNS latency returned to <5ms with 0% dropped UDP packets?
submission_fields.guidance: Define CoreDNS metrics and conntrack table saturation thresholds.

submission_fields.label: 5. Preventative Follow-up Action
submission_fields.placeholder: What cluster-wide architectural change (e.g. NodeLocal DNSCache) prevents this permanently?
submission_fields.guidance: Consider NodeLocal DNSCache daemonset and pod dnsConfig tuning.

dimensions.name: Evidence Accuracy
dimensions.criteria: Correctly links conntrack table saturation (262,144 limit) and ndots:5 generating 4 NXDOMAIN queries per external call.

dimensions.name: Plausibility & Fact/Assumption Clarity
dimensions.criteria: Explains the glibc ndots DNS lookup mechanics accurately, separating UDP packet drops from node CPU capacity.

dimensions.name: Safe Mitigation Plan
dimensions.criteria: Safely increases kernel conntrack sysctl max, scales CoreDNS replicas, or appends trailing dot (api.stripe.com.) in client configurations.

dimensions.name: Verification & Preventive Engineering
dimensions.criteria: Monitors CoreDNS p99 latency < 5ms; deploys Kubernetes NodeLocal DNSCache DaemonSet for local link caching.
